title: Roadmap Launch Readiness - Engineering Planning
summary: Internal engineering planning for launch readiness of the Q4 roadmap items: finalize latency SLOs, incident runbook updates, staging benchmark plan, and rollouts for Dedicated and Private launch features. Agreed next steps include a perf benchmark on staging, a runbook dry-run, and a final checklist by product before go/no-go.
topics: Incident runbook updates and drill schedule
Docs and internal comms for launch
transcript:
[00:00] Aisha (PM): okay, good morning team, thanks for squeezing this in, I know it's a busy week. main goal today is to go through the launch readiness checklist and make sure eng has what it needs for the Q4 push. we have 75 minutes but we'll try to keep tight
[01:12] Carlos (Eng): yeah, I skimmed the checklist, a couple of items i want to call out - the latency SLOs and the staging perf harness. we found some regressions on long sequences last week.
[02:03] Leah (SRE): and the incident runbook needs a refresh after the kv cache outage we had two sprints ago; some of the steps are outdated, and the escalation matrix needs to include on-call for dedicated infra.
[03:05] Ravi (Tech Lead): quick clarifying question, are we shipping dedicated and private at the same time or staggered? because that changes the rollout plan and the dependencies on KMS/HSM integrations.
[03:40] Aisha: product wants parallel-ish, but marketing prefers a staged announcement. operationally we should probably stagger: dedicated first, then private once KMS and audit logs are validated.
[04:20] Marcus (Product Ops): agreed, and legal also asked for an attestation doc for the private package, so that needs to be ready.
[05:15] Speaker 1: (mumble) we should verify the SSO docs too, SAML flow was flaky in the last run.
[06:00] Carlos: notes - SSO, KMS, audit logs. for latency SLOs we're proposing p50 60ms, p95 220ms, p99 480ms on our beefy staging infra. those are targets for hosted. Dedicated is higher since multi-tenant contends less, dedicated we can aim for p50 45ms, p95 180ms. someone correct me if i'm off.
[07:05] Leah: that sounds reasonable; i want to see the distribution from the last 10k requests though, the tail is spikier when we hit long context. also need to review batching settings - some of the regressions came from a change in continuous batching parameters.
[08:30] Ravi: right, continuous batching tuning changed; i think the default max_batch_delay was bumped which increased latency under low qps. we should include batching profiles per route in the checklist.
[09:45] Aisha: action: include batching profile per route (Aisha to add to doc). next, staging benchmarks. Carlos, can eng run the end-to-end perf harness using the real eval prompts?
[10:30] Carlos: yes, we can. we'll need the eval set that Marcus mentioned; i think there was an updated prompt set from the spec review. Marcus, can you share link to the spreadsheet?
[11:05] Marcus: i'll share after call - it's the latest 'q4-launch-prompts.xlsx' in the /shared drive. note some prompts are high token counts, may spike seq length.
[12:00] Carlos: good. we'll run three campaigns: baseline (current main), candidate-quantized, and candidate-kernel-optim. need to watch memory/oom on long sequences.
[12:40] Leah: also we should test KV cache warm starts, because cache miss storms caused the outage last time. add a scenario for cold-start with many small requests to simulate churn.
[13:30] Ravi: we also still have the open item for the kernel selection fallback - if the optimized kernel fails on a given GPU, we need automatic fallback to the compatibility path without dropping the request. is that implemented?
[14:05] Carlos: partial - fallback exists, but it's not surfaced in metrics well. we'll add telemetry for fallback counts and latency delta.
[15:00] Speaker 2: (overlap) can we add a trace id that surfaces in the console for any fallback event? that'd help triage.
[15:25] Leah: yes, we can tag the trace and surface in console traces; i need a small schema for the trace fields.
[16:00] Aisha: okay good. i want to touch incident runbook next. Leah, you flagged the escalation matrix. what do you need from engineering?
[16:30] Leah: need clear owners per service - runtime, routing, cache, and infra. we need the on-call rotation documented and a dry-run scheduled. propose dry-run week of Oct 19.
[17:05] Carlos: that works for eng. also want an SLA playbook for capacity alerts - if dedicated pool drops below 60% we want automatic spillover to hosted for critical customers. is that policy in the checklist?
[17:50] Aisha: it's listed as 'fallback policy' but we need concrete thresholds. let's set threshold proposals: spillover at 60% sustained for 2 minutes; alerting at 75% for 1 minute. open to adjustments.
[18:35] Ravi: can the spillover be per-tenant or is it global? per-tenant is safer to avoid noisy neighbors.
[18:55] Leah: technically we can do per-tenant routing policy, but it requires route-time decisions and tagging. we'll need to define the tag schema.
[19:20] Marcus: i'll add route tag schema to the checklist and coordinate with docs.
[20:00] Speaker 3: uh, there's also the compliance checklist for private customers - SOC2 controls mapping for the private package. Legal wants an inventory of logs retained and where keys are stored.
[20:45] Aisha: good point. we need a short one-pager for compliance with retention windows and KMS locations. Ravi, can you confirm the HSM integration status?
[21:10] Ravi: HSM POC completed, but still on staging. production rollout for HSM needs partner sign-off and a migration plan - estimate two weeks once we schedule.
[21:50] Carlos: for the staging benchmarks, what's the expected acceptance criteria? e.g., no p99 regressions > 10% vs baseline and no OOMs in 1000-long sequence tests.
[22:25] Aisha: yep, acceptance criteria: p99 delta <= 10% vs baseline, no memory errors in stress tests, and feature flags for rollback. also monitors and alerts configured.
[23:10] Leah: monitors: latency SLI dashboards, fallback telemetry, cache hit ratios, and pod eviction counts. we'll add runbook links to each monitor.
[24:00] Marcus: marketing needs feature descriptions and a launch one-pager by Oct 23. we should sync with them on staging screenshots and performance numbers they can cite.
[24:40] Aisha: ok add comms deliverables. next, docs. who's owning the public-facing runbook?
[25:10] Ravi: i can own the technical runbook, but docs will need review from support and product.
[25:40] Marcus: support asked for a triage flow doc for customers during a degradation event. they'll contribute examples.
[26:05] Aisha: scheduling - can we align on a dry-run timeline? Leah suggested week of Oct 19 for the incident drill, Carlos will run perf by Oct 16, Marcus will deliver prompt set by Oct 13, and i will compile the final checklist by Oct 14.
[26:45] Carlos: i have a note - we need to coordinate with infra to reserve staging cluster for bench runs; otherwise noisy tests will collide. Leah, can you open a provisioning ticket?
[27:10] Leah: yes, I'll request a staging slot and tag it 'q4-launch-bench'.
[27:35] Speaker 1: (mutter) also verify that the billing meter won't be skewed during bench runs, we don't want cost surprises.
[28:05] Carlos: good catch. we'll route bench traffic through test billing account.
[28:40] Aisha: risks - what are the top three risks for launch?
[29:00] Ravi: 1) kernel regressions on long-context workloads; 2) KMS/HSM production readiness delay; 3) telemetry gaps for fallback and cache events.
[29:35] Leah: agree, add 4) incident response coordination across dedicated/private teams.
[30:00] Marcus: mitigation for kernel regressions: candidate run with compatibility fallback enabled and perf gates; for KMS, accelerate partner sign-off; telemetry gaps - add trace id and fallback counters.
[30:40] Aisha: ok. let's talk MVP scope - anything in backlog that must be cut?
[31:05] Carlos: we should postpone advanced autoscaling features (predictive scale) from launch; leave basic autoscale and burst capacity.
[31:40] Leah: also postpone 3rd party audit integration until after launch.
[32:10] Aisha: good. now let's capture explicit next steps and owners.
[32:30] Marcus: i'll share prompts link and a short marketing milestone doc by Oct 13.
[32:50] Carlos: eng will run perf campaigns on staging and post results by Oct 16. will include fallback telemetry instrumentation.
[33:10] Leah: i'll update the incident runbook and schedule dry-run for Oct 19; will also raise provisioning ticket for staging.
[33:40] Ravi: i'll finalize HSM migration plan and confirm whether it's 2 weeks post-sign-off, target update by Oct 18.
[34:05] Aisha: i'll compile the final readiness checklist and circulate by Oct 14. also set a go/no-go review on Oct 22.
[34:40] Speaker 2: (quiet) we should also update the console to show per-route batching profiles in config view.
[35:05] Carlos: noted, UI ticket to product; Marcus will prioritize.
[35:40] Aisha: any blockers from anyone?
[35:55] Marcus: legal review for private package attestation might take longer; will chase.
[36:20] Leah: none from SRE beyond what we discussed.
[36:40] Ravi: slight resource constraint if kernel debugging takes longer, but we'll escalate.
[37:00] Aisha: ok, recap, next steps will be captured and i'll send the checklist; meeting over if nobody has anything else. thanks all.
[37:25] Carlos: thanks.
[37:30] Leah: thanks everyone.
[37:35] (call ends)
